title: Telemetry-driven Dedicated Reserve Autoscaler PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated customers reserve GPU capacity but experience wasted headroom during low demand and sudden latency spikes during transient traffic bursts. Existing burst handoffs are manual or coarse-grained, leading to either over-provisioned commitments (high cost) or frequent fallback to hosted models (poor SLAs).

Opportunity: Use rich runtime telemetry (instance-level utilization, queue length, prefix cache hit rate, per-tenant token rate) to drive an autoscaling layer that dynamically shifts reserved capacity windows and temporary micro-reserves while honoring isolation policies and preemption contracts. The system should reduce cost for customers that underutilize reservations while improving effective SLOs during microbursts.

High-level solution: Build a telemetry-driven autoscaler for Dedicated reserved pools that: 1) continuously computes safe headroom reclaims and micro-reserve bids for tenants, 2) exposes opt-in policy controls (min_alloc, burst_credit, preemptibility), and 3) integrates with the routing layer to pre-warm or borrow capacity with transparent billing adjustments and audit logs.

This PRD documents requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and open questions for the initial MVP focused on single-zone reserved pools and per-tenant burst credits.
goals: Reduce average idle reserved capacity across pilot tenants by 20% without increasing P95 latency beyond SLOs
Provide opt-in tenant controls for minimum allocation and burstability with deterministic billing and audit trail
Enable automated short-lived micro-reserves (1-30m) that can be reclaimed with configurable grace windows
Produce telemetry and dashboards that explain autoscaler decisions and provide backfill/eviction audit logs
non_goals: Replacing long-term contractual reservations or renegotiating committed capacity
Cross-zone rebalancing in the initial MVP
Transparent multi-tenant GPU sharing at the kernel level (no novel kernel multiplexing)
assumptions: High-fidelity telemetry (1m granularity) for per-tenant token rates, queue depth, and instance utilization is available
Routing layer can support temporary route overrides and prewarm signals for specific model variants
Billing system can record sub-minute adjustments and apply usage-based reconciliation for micro-reserves
requirements: Functional: Autoscaler must compute a per-pool reclaimable headroom estimate every minute and publish suggested micro-reserve slots
Functional: Expose policy surface: min_alloc (absolute tokens/s or fraction), max_burst_duration, burst_priority, preemptable=true/false
Functional: Create audit events for every headroom reclaim, micro-reserve grant, and preemption decision stored for 90 days
Functional: Integrate with Console to show per-tenant headroom, recent autoscale actions, and simulated cost savings
Functional: Provide a dry-run mode and opt-in toggle per tenant (default off for existing customers)
Non-functional: Compute decisions within the 1-minute cadence with end-to-end decision latency < 5s from telemetry snapshot to route change
Non-functional: Autoscaler should not cause more than 1% additional request rejections for tenants during normal operation
Non-functional: System must support pilot pools up to 200 nodes and scale horizontally for future rollout
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry pipeline: Grafana dashboard shows per-pool reclaimable headroom and matches ground-truth within ±10% for 95% of samples over a 48h window
Policy enforcement: A pilot tenant can set min_alloc and get guaranteed baseline throughput even when headroom reclaims occur
Micro-reserve behavior: When a micro-reserve is granted, end-to-end latency (P95) for the tenant remains within 1.2x their SLO for the first 5 minutes; then returns to baseline
Preemption safety: If a higher-priority tenant triggers preemption, lower-priority micro-reserves are reclaimed within the configured grace window and logged; no silent dropouts
Cost reconciliation: Billing shows micro-reserve usage as distinct line items and matches simulated cost reduction within 5% for pilot tenants over a 7-day test
Rollout controls: Feature flag enables per-organization opt-in; dry-run mode emits identical audit logs without affecting routing
Observability: At least three autoscaler decision types (reclaim, micro-reserve-grant, preempt) have end-to-end traces and associated GitHub actions/PR links in Console
design_notes: Autoscaler will operate in two modes: conservative (minimal reclaims, safe defaults) and aggressive (higher reclaim aggressiveness for agreed pilot customers). Decision engine uses a weighted scoring function combining recent utilization, cache-hit-rate, and queue-growth velocity. Use sealed bidding for micro-reserve grants: tenants with available burst_credit can be preferentially granted micro-reserves up to max_burst_duration. All decision logic versioned and stored to ensure regression testing.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal sandbox (week 1): run autoscaler in dry-run against synthetic load; 2) Pilot customers (weeks 2-4): opt-in small set of enterprise tenants in a single zone with conservative policy; 3) Expand to additional pools and aggressive mode A/B tests (weeks 5-8); 4) Full GA gate once telemetry, billing, and SLO stability validated. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria checks and a go/no-go checklist reviewed by SRE and Security.
metrics: Number of micro-reserves granted per day
Fraction of reclaims that led to customer-visible fallback
Billing reconciliation delta between simulated and actual costs
stakeholders: Marco Chen - Engineering Lead, Dedicated Runtime
risks: Telemetry inaccuracy causing unsafe reclaims: mitigated by conservative mode and dry-run
Billing edge-cases leading to customer confusion: mitigate with explicit line items and communications
Preemption races causing request failures: mitigate with grace windows and route draining hooks
Customer mistrust of automatic reclaims: provide transparency, audit logs, and opt-out
open_questions: What is the minimum viable grace window length for preemption to avoid request failures (30s vs 2m)?
Should burst_credit be transferrable between pools in the same org?
How should micro-reserve billing be apportioned if a reserve is preempted mid-minute?
Does Security require HSM-level signing for autoscaler audit events?
